There was hostility to Franklin in Congress, partly due to irritation from Adams and others regarding Franklin's reputation in France.

Franklin had enemies during the long contests in Pennsylvania, particularly among the wealth and rank of the province, and there remains an hereditary antipathy to him in a certain circle in Philadelphia.
Franklin experienced acrimony with Thomas and Richard Penn, and he seems to have disliked their father as well.
The natural abhorrence which tory courtiers entertained for Franklin influenced the government's subsequent course toward him.

Benjamin Franklin is widely known for his discoveries in electricity, particularly the popular image of his kite experiment, which is often cited as the main thing people remember about his contributions to science.
His reputation was greatly enhanced by his discoveries in electricity, making his name well known in both America and Europe, and he became a household word from Boston to Charleston.
Franklin's fame was further increased by the invention of the lightning-rod, which was considered most important in building up his reputation.
He was also celebrated for his writings, such as Poor Richard's maxims, which were widely known and translated, and for his clear and modest scientific letters.
Franklin invented the lightning-rod and explained its action in a paper sent to Collinson.
He invented the invaluable contrivance by which a fire consumes its own smoke.
Franklin made important discoveries respecting the causes of colds.
He discovered the temperature of the Gulf stream and that Northeast storms begin in the Southwest.
Franklin invented the 'Pennsylvania Fireplace,' which was an improvement on old methods of heating and ventilation.

Franklin lived in the little village of Passy, about two miles from the heart of Paris, for nine years, where his famous letters were dated and he resided in part of the Hotel de Valentinois as his home and for the business of the embassy free of rent.

Franklin spent five years in England on his mission, settled with his own servant and living in the Craven Street house, and his grandson Temple lived there with him during his second mission to England and accompanied him to France.
Franklin established himself at Passy, in a court of the Hotel de Valentinois, and continued to reside there during his whole stay in France, maintaining an independent establishment.
Franklin visited Paris in September 1767, and the year preceding he had been in Germany, accompanied by Sir John Pringle.
Franklin lived in London for a year and a half before embarking for Philadelphia.

Franklin had a new house built during his absence, and after his return, his daughter Mrs. Sarah Bache was mistress of it; he arrived on the 5th of May, 1775, and was occupied in Philadelphia until October 26, 1776, when he sailed for France.

Benjamin Franklin had a peculiar fondness for swimming and retained his boyish skill in it to old age, even inventing swimming aids such as oval pallets for his hands and sandals for his feet, which he described in a letter to a friend later in life.
He complained that he never could acquire the virtue of order in his business, having a place for everything and everything in its place, and this failing followed him to the end of his life.

A few days before he died, Benjamin Franklin rose from his bed and begged that it might be made up for him so that he might die in a decent manner, and he calmly replied to his daughter, who hoped he would recover, 'I hope not.'
He died with cheerfulness and peace, leaving behind him a mass of writings, full of his own kindness, humor, and wisdom, to perpetuate his influence and sweeten the life of coming generations.

The Congress of the United States passed a resolution for members to wear the customary badge of mourning for one month as a mark of veneration due to his memory, and the National Assembly of France paid him distinguished honors upon his death.

Boston showed appreciation for Benjamin Franklin by naming a square after him and erecting monuments in his honor, and sixty-six years after his death, his native city celebrated his memory with banquets, illuminations, and fireworks.
